source.title: Genesis Steering: Better Activation Steering Through Training Data
source.authors: Tora Bodin; Eric Aubinais; Ilaria Torre; Chih-Hong Cheng

page_placements.theme: Directions and maps other than DIM also control refusal; DIM is not the unique or optimal handle

record.file_problem: The text is a full paper; no truncation or garbling apparent.
record.tranche_reason: It uses difference-of-means refusal vectors and tests behavioral steering by adding or subtracting a vector at a chosen layer. It does not perform the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper tests steering with vectors derived from several datasets and membership-selected subsets, reporting behavior-flip measures. It does not ablate the direction, make a weight edit, or assess general capability preservation. Theoretical propositions are not empirical model outcomes. Membership-ranking/AUC results and cited findings are not rows because they do not report steering behavior.
record.test_reason: The study builds harmful/refusal-minus-benign/compliance difference-of-means vectors and steers two 8B chat models with them at one layer (input of block 16). Subtracting the vector makes models comply on HarmBench and StrongREJECT. Adding it makes them refuse on XSTest, OR-Bench and Alpaca. A random direction serves as a control. This bears on V1's induce/remove claim by a different method: additive steering at one site rather than all-layer directional ablation. The study's focus is which data define the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that reference data matter: Tülu-3-8B's safety-mixture datasets yield stronger difference-of-means steering vectors than external datasets on both Tülu-3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Membership-based selection recovers Tülu's training data and gives vectors competitive with random subsets, but hurts steering on Llama. They attribute this to selection shifting the class means more than it reduces bias.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the difference-of-means residual-stream vector and additive steering, but tests a selected layer/site rather than projection from every layer and position. Vectors come from multiple safety datasets or membership-selected proxies; vectors are normalized and swept over doses.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering outcome changes with reference dataset and with membership selection; the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct Min-K%++ top selection is a pronounced low-steerability case. Experiments use layer 16 and fixed prompt positions; no layer or position sensitivity result is reported as a final comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: CAA refusal vectors, built from contrasting authored answers to the same question, steer refusal no better than or only modestly above a random direction: S 0.168/0.459 on Tülu and 0.033/0.089 on Llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Response-style contrast vectors (same prompt, refusing vs complying answer) do not recover the refusal direction that instruction-contrast vectors give.

record.problems: Only two 8B models sharing a base, one steering layer/site, English safety datasets, and a single LLM judge are used. The authors state that standard errors capture prompt-sampling variability but not judge or decoding variability. Steering can cause degeneration at higher doses; the membership-proxy Min-K%++ top selection on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct loses 0.409 of prompts to degeneration. The study does not test the all-layer ablation or general-capability preservation claims.
record.rows_left_out: No outcome rows omitted from the reported empirical steering results used here. Membership ranking, score AUC, and activation-geometry analyses were not included because they do not themselves report the target behavioral steering outcome.

untested.parts: Directional ablation or projection at every layer and position; whether the direction is necessary for unsteered refusal; general-capability preservation on standard benchmarks (only degeneration shares are reported); models other than two Llama-3.1-8B derivatives; layers other than 16 (a layer sweep is mentioned without numbers).
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial-training analysis.
No multi-direction or cone analysis. Cosines between dataset vectors (about 0.63–0.79) are reported but not framed as refusal dimensionality.
No direction is transferred across models, languages or base-to-instruct. Each model's vector is computed from its own activations.
The paper suggests training-data composition shapes steering directions but runs no training manipulation. The safety-free twin model is used only for membership scoring.

missing.what: 'CoCoNot, both poles from Tülu's mixture' vector: S 0.658 (Tülu) and 0.552 (Llama), jailbreak range 0.342/0.331. A dataset-dependent weak case for V1.

Unsteered baselines per benchmark. Compliance on HarmBench is 0.03 (Tülu) and 0.11 (Llama); refusal on XSTest is 0.16/0.13, on OR-Bench 0.46/0.32, on Alpaca 0.01/0.00. These are needed to read flip ranges.

Dose-response degeneration: at high doses most responses degenerate (e.g. ≥0.7 degenerate at |α|=10–12 on HarmBench). The lost-to-degeneration share per vector is a proxy for the capability cost V1 says is small.

record.verdict_notes: V6 is dropped: the Llama rows recompute the vector on Llama's own activations, so nothing transfers between models. Both models share the Llama-3.1-8B base. T3 proxy rows mainly compare the study's own selection method and are kept as V1 evidence only as generic difference-of-means vectors. CAA rows are relinked to none because they contrast responses, not instructions. Evaluation relies on one LLM judge (gemma-2-27b-it) with reported agreement of κ≈0.70–0.74, one layer, and greedy decoding. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No projection/ablation of the direction; no intervention at every layer and position; no test that the direction mediates unsteered refusal; no separate evaluation of general capability preservation.
Transfer is tested only between two 8B models sharing the Llama-3.1-8B base, using English datasets and one steering site; no language transfer or base-to-instruct transfer test.

relation.reason: Reports refusal-removal and refusal-induction rates for difference-of-means vectors from many datasets on two models, with a random-direction control. These results bear on V1.

tranche.reason: Same question, different method: additive subtraction/addition of a unit-normalized difference-of-means vector at one site (input of block 16), not directional ablation. Results are flip rates against a random-direction control.

source_check.notes: A prompt counts as flipped if any dose flips it (nominal |α| up to 12 harmful / 8 benign; E.4 says 0.5 steps). 100 prompts per benchmark, one judge (gemma-2-27b-it), no capability benchmark. Per Appendix C the CoCoNot† compliance pole is not in Tülu's mixture. The 'both poles from mixture' CoCoNot vector steers worse (S 0.658 Tülu, 0.552 Llama).

statements.correction: S 0.990: WildGuardMix, Tülu-3-8B. Do-Not-Answer: 0.730 on Tülu-3-8B, 0.667 on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Min-K%++ top-128: 0.489 vs random subsets 0.943 on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (0.409 of prompts lost to degeneration; selection source-skewed). Same selection on Tülu-3-8B: 0.974 vs 0.966. Random direction: 0.182 (Tülu), 0.083 (Llama).
statements.problem: The 0.990, 0.730, 0.667, 0.489 and 0.943 values are all in the text. But the Min-K%++ comparison is on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct only and the sentence names only Tülu-3-8B. On Tülu the same selection steers as well as random subsets. The framing that selection 'decides whether it mediates refusal' is also too strong here: every dataset vector stays far above the random direction.

statements.correction: Random direction S: 0.182 ± 0.018 on Tülu-3-8B, 0.083 ± 0.014 on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Table 17). Seven dataset vectors: S 0.667-0.990, all far above random (0.867-0.990 only if DNA and Llama PKU are excluded). Random direction still flips some prompts: Tülu jailbreak 0.117, over-ref 0.247. All vectors are unit-normalized, at the same doses. Rows: T17-TULU-RANDOMDIR, T17-LLAMA-RANDOMDIR.
statements.problem: The random-direction values are right. The comparison range 0.867-0.990 leaves out the weaker dataset vectors: Do-Not-Answer on both models and PKU-SafeRLHF on Llama. The cited row id T3-LLAMA-RANDOMDIR does not exist; the random-direction rows are the T17 ones.

statements.correction: 0.990: WildGuardMix on Tülu-3-8B. 0.667: Do-Not-Answer on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Per model: Tülu 0.730-0.990, Llama 0.667-0.960.
statements.problem: The range is right, but its two ends are on different models. Do-Not-Answer is an external dataset, not a genesis dataset.
